summary: Faz 9 CP4.35 P1 fix validation + full regression. Backend: 56/56 iter60-64 regression suite GREEN (test_tasks_locks + test_tasks_lock_audit + test_tasks_user_policy + test_lock_policy_templates + test_p0_cp434). P1 new suite (test_p1_cp435.py, 11 tests): 10 PASS, 1 FAIL (locked_by attribution). P1 verifications: (1) Template validation — 81-char name → 400 'en fazla 80 karakter' ✓; 501-char description → 400 '500' ✓; empty name → 400 ✓; valid → 201 ✓; PATCH name>80 → 400 ✓. (2) Cap enforcement — manager filled to exactly 50 templates, 51st → 400 with '50 şablon' text ✓; admin cap independent from manager (admin can add template while mgr at 50) ✓. (3) delete_task used_otp — (a) admin deletes unlocked task → audit used_otp=false ✓; (b) ahmet has lock_edit=true + active OTP window but delete NOT locked → deletes → used_otp=false ✓ (this is the CP4.35 fix — previously would falsely be true); (c) ahmet with lock_delete=true + verified OTP → deletes → used_otp=true ✓. (4) Double inherit — managed lock_flags = {lock_delete, lock_edit} correct; self_lock_flags = {lock_complete} (lock_delete deduped, managed wins) correct; locked_at set correct. FAILURE: locked_by attribution — when ahmet self-patches AFTER admin's managed patch, task inherits locked_by=ahmet instead of admin. RCA: patch_user_lock_flags writes default_lock_set_by_user_id in BOTH channels (managed branch + self branch), so a subsequent self patch overwrites the managed policy owner. create_task then reads that single field and mis-attributes the managed lock. Frontend smoke: admin serkan login OK, dashboard renders (SERTEX title, weather 27.9°C, task counter 4/5, memory/notes panels), no active error banners on page. No console errors during login+dashboard render.

minor.issue: locked_by attribution for MANAGED inherited lock is overwritten to whoever last patched user policy — including the assignee's own self-lock patch. RCA: patch_user_lock_flags stores default_lock_set_by_user_id as a SINGLE shared field regardless of channel (managed vs self), so admin sets it → ahmet self-patches → field now = ahmet → next created task's managed lock is attributed to ahmet. Break: audit trail lies about who set the strict lock; assignee appears to have imposed lock on themselves. Fix: store default_lock_set_by_user_id per channel (e.g. default_lock_managed_set_by_user_id vs default_lock_self_set_by_user_id) and read the managed one in create_task. Verified: task with ONLY managed patch (no self) correctly attributes locked_by=admin — so the fix works in isolation, breaks only under the double-inherit scenario.

action_items: FIX P1 locked_by attribution regression: split default_lock_set_by_user_id into two channel-scoped fields (managed vs self) OR only write it in the managed branch. Currently the assignee's own self-lock patch corrupts the managed-lock policy-owner attribution. See tasks_router.py:1241-1248 (patch_user_lock_flags) and :522 (create_task inheritance).
critical_code_review_comments: tasks_router.py:522 — `t.locked_by = policy_doc.get('default_lock_set_by_user_id') or user['id']`. The read source is a single mutable field shared with the self-lock channel — see :1241 & :1247. Any assignee self-patch overwrites the managed policy owner. Recommended: `default_lock_managed_set_by_user_id` for strict channel, `default_lock_self_set_by_user_id` for self channel; create_task reads only the managed one.

tasks_router.py:639 — delete_task audit `used_otp` computation is now correct: only checks if the delete action itself was locked (was_delete_locked = lock_delete OR self_lock_delete). Prior bug fixed. Good.

tasks_router.py:1315-1335 — template validation is airtight (empty/81+/501+/cap 100 admin, 50 manager, per-creator via count_documents with created_by filter). No SQL-inject-style bypass surface since values pass through Pydantic then re-stripped/measured.

TasksPanel.jsx:207-254 — playReminderBeep returns proper `{cancel}` handle that clears BOTH secondBeepTimer and closeTimer + closes AudioContext. Race-safe against unmount. beep() wrapper (:2562) tracks in activeBeepsRef Set, cleanup useEffect (:2556) cancels all on unmount. Solid implementation.

Manager cap 50 is enforced per-creator using created_by index scan; existing tests confirm independence between creators. However list_lock_policy_templates returns ALL templates to any manager — under a heavy multi-tenant deployment consider filtering to created_by = self OR company scope.

rca of the issue: Double-inherit locked_by regression: patch_user_lock_flags (tasks_router.py:1220-1252) has two mutually-exclusive branches (is_self+non-admin/mgr → self channel, else → managed channel), but BOTH write `default_lock_set_by_user_id: user['id']` into the users doc. This single field is then read at create_task (:522) as the policy-owner for the MANAGED lock only. When admin sets managed and ahmet later sets self, the field ends up as ahmet's id; a new task's managed lock gets attributed to ahmet (the assignee), misleading the audit trail. Repro: PATCH /users/{eid}/lock-flags as admin with managed flags → PATCH /users/{eid}/lock-flags as ahmet with self flags → POST /tasks (assignee=ahmet) → task.locked_by == ahmet.id (WRONG, should be admin.id). Mitigation: introduce channel-specific attribution fields OR only write default_lock_set_by_user_id in the managed branch (self channel doesn't need attribution since it's owner-managed by definition).
